lead.answer: You write a small JSON file; build.py turns it into one checked HTML page.
points: The top-level key picks the page: `panels`, `views` or `flows`.
Every page goes through check.py, and an ERROR stops the hand-over.
Flow pages have their own module, flow.py, because they need layout.

views.label: Build
views.summary: What happens when you run `python3 scripts/build.py page.json`.

steps.title: The builder reads the spec and picks the page kind.
steps.body: One key in the spec decides the layout. No other setting does.

path.what: Anything else is a sheet of lettered `panels`.

steps.title: Each panel or step holds exactly one exhibit.
steps.body: The exhibit key names the drawing. Two keys in one panel stop the build.

steps.title: The builder inlines the CSS and writes one file.
steps.body: The page needs no other file. Fonts come from Google Fonts; without them the system font shows.

path.what: Reads `assets/sheet.css` and puts it in a style tag.
Runs `check.py` and exits with its code.

steps.title: Style problems only warn.
steps.body: A warning prints a line and the page still builds. Fix it before you hand the page over.

decisions.choice: A JSON spec plus premade CSS
decisions.why: The same checks and both themes apply to every page.

decisions.choice: Flow layout in Python at build time
decisions.why: No install, and the build can count crossings before hand-over.
